chapter: Barnet, 52nd Street and New York recording dates
title: Tadd Dameron's "Good Beat" and the Cozy Cole date
summary: He made "Good Beat" with Dizzy and led-by-Cozy date with Hawkins, Earl Hines, Joe Thomas and Billy Taylor, including his tune "Through for the Night."

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Was that the only time you recorded with Bird and Diz, or did you do it other times?
No, I did some other little things like --

-- 'Can't Get Started,' and then I did a record -- I don't know if Byrd was on there, but I know Diz was on it. It was Tadd Dameron's 'Good Beat.' I did that, the first recording ever on 'Good Beat,' I did.

I don't remember. We never paid any attention to the labels, but I know Teddy Reed used to get quite a few of those things together, and then Harry Lim used to get a lot of those -- Little dates together, because I remember I did a recording with Cozy Cole, myself, Coleman Hawkins, Earl Hines, guy named Billy Taylor on bass, Joe Thomas on trumpet, and I forgot who was the -- who was the drums on that date. I forgot. Cozy was the drummer.
And it came out under Cozy's name. We did some things through for the --
We were talking on the last reel the record date in which Cozy was the leader. about (inaudible).

That's right. This was a date Harry put together in New York, and Cozy was leader on it, and, as I mentioned, four of the guy -- guys in the group was Coleman Hawkins, Earl Hines, Billy Taylor on bass -- he's a bass player. I think he retired. He played with Duke once. And myself and Joe Thomas on trumpet, and it was a good date. We did one song I wrote, was "Through for the Night." And then we did Blue Moon, and then we featured Earl and Coleman Hawkins on "Just One More Chance." And I don't remember what -- I don't remember what the other song was. We did four sides on that. And that was a late date too. But it was a good recording because I remember Hawk was in good form that night, and Joe Thomas always was a good trumpet player. You know, he was playing real nice back then. And I enjoyed the date. Earl played real good, and Billy Taylor was a fine bass man. I knew him way back with Duke's band, always enjoyed his work. But this was a good date. I haven't heard these recordings in many years now, but I had -- I had the recording at one time. It's been a long time ago, though, since we did those things.
